summary: Interleaved GPU fairness degradation in dedicated pool causing mid-day throughput collapse for BrightWrite Labs
description: Issue summary: During the 11:30-14:30 UTC window on 2026-03-12 BrightWrite Labs observed a sudden drop in sustained throughput from their dedicated GPU pool. Requests that previously sustained ~2800 tokens/s dropped to ~900 tokens/s and p99 latency spiked. Support was notified by the customer after service-level alerts fired. Impact: customer-facing inference traffic experienced elevated latency and increased error retry rates; some production jobs hit per-tenant throttling fallback and fell back to smaller model variants, degrading result quality.
timeline: 2026-03-12 11:28 UTC - BrightWrite monitoring: p99 latency rising from ~320ms to 1.8s
2026-03-12 11:35 UTC - Customer opened ticket and sent traces to support; attached SDK trace IDs

2026-03-12 12:15 UTC - Observed GPU allocation failures (driver warnings) for 2 nodes, followed by soft-evictions
2026-03-12 12:40 UTC - Applied temporary request throttling for other noisy tenants in same reserved pool to isolate impact

steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightWrite customer credentials to replay production traffic profile (bursting short streams with long context pinning).
2) Target dedicated pool us-east reserved slice at peak window (11:00-14:00 UTC).
3) Observe autoscaler behavior under short high-frequency bursts and subsequent slot fragmentation.
4) Capture GPU allocation events and serving-runtime batcher logs for noise patterns.
logs: [2026-03-12T12:09:12.102Z] metrics: brightwrite p50=180ms p95=920ms p99=1798ms throughput_tokens_per_s=920
metrics_snapshot: Incident peak: p50=180ms p95=920ms p99=1.8s, tokens/s=900
GPU utilization across pool: avg_gpu_util=76%, tail_gpu_io_wait=14% (spike to 48% on two nodes)
Autoscaler events: 3 rebalances in 18 minutes; each shrink triggered prefetch eviction metric thresholds
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Noisy neighbor (short, high-rate streams) caused slot fragmentation and increased scheduler churn; small streams occupied batcher slots preventing efficient batching for BrightWrite bursts.
Hypothesis 2: KV cache growth for the noisy tenant caused HBM pressure on specific GPUs and triggered the scheduler to migrate/evict, creating allocation latency cascades.
Hypothesis 3: Autoscaler smoothing window too aggressive for workloads with high short-term variance; shrink decisions applied before traffic pattern stabilized, causing under-provisioning.
Evidence: logs show KVCacheGrow + driver IO_WAIT spikes correlated with the throttle window; batcher_hold events for other tenants coincide with BrightWrite latency rise.
Telemetry gaps: need deeper GPU perf counters for nvlink/dma stalls at 1s granularity and batcher slot occupancy traces for the timeframe.
Cross-references: see Slack thread #support-brightwrite (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02BR1T5K) and perf PR github.com/redwood/realtime-serv/PR-3421 for proposed batcher backpressure fix.
SRE note: two nodes had repeated soft-evictions but hardware diagnostics returned healthy; likely scheduling/IO contention rather than driver crash.
actions_taken: 2026-03-12 12:40 UTC - Applied soft throttle to identified noisy tenant (other-tenant-901) within the same reserved pool to reduce short-stream fanout.
2026-03-12 12:50 UTC - Temporarily increased autoscaler min_slots for BrightWrite slice to reduce shrink events during bursts.
2026-03-12 13:05 UTC - Isolated persistent noisy processes to a separate slice and marked for follow-up eviction policy change.
2026-03-13 09:00 UTC - Collected extended GPU perf counters and batcher traces for the incident window; uploaded to S3: s3://perf-archive/sup-777777/archives.tar.gz
2026-03-14 09:30 UTC - Implemented temporary autoscaler smoothing parameter change in staging for A/B testing: smoothing_window=60s -> 180s (PR-3421).

resolution: Partial workaround applied: noisy tenant isolated and soft-throttled which restored most throughput for BrightWrite. Autoscaler smoothing change deployed to staging for validation. Permanent fixes planned: 1) Add per-tenant short-stream detection to avoid slot hogging, 2) Increase autoscaler smoothing and add hysteresis for shrink decisions, 3) Add HBM pressure signal to eviction heuristics. Follow-ups assigned to platform-eng (PR-3421) and INT-9021 for instrumentation. Customer notified and will receive postmortem after root-cause confirmation.
